articles.title: How Does a Microwave Heat Your Food?
articles.dek: There is no fire inside a microwave. So how does your soup get hot?
paras: Many families have got a microwave oven in their kitchen. You put in some cold soup, press a button and wait. After two minutes, the soup is hot! But how does it work? There isn't any fire inside a microwave. It doesn't get red and hot like a normal oven. So where does the heat come from?

The answer is microwaves. A microwave is a kind of invisible wave, a bit like a radio wave. A small machine inside the oven makes them. It is called a magnetron. The waves move around inside the metal box very fast. They go into the food, but only about two or three centimetres deep.

Most food has got a lot of water in it. There is water in fruit, vegetables, rice and soup. The microwaves make the tiny bits of water in the food move very fast. When they move fast, they get hot. Then the heat goes into the rest of the food.

Have you ever looked at the round plate inside a microwave? It turns slowly while the food cooks. The waves don't reach every part of the oven in the same way. So the plate moves the food around, and more of it gets hot. But sometimes there are still some cold parts in your food. Then you should stir it and heat it again for a few seconds.

Don't put any metal in a microwave! A fork or a piece of foil can make sparks. Sparks are very small flashes of light, and they can be dangerous. Use a glass bowl or a plate with a "microwave safe" sign.

Who invented the microwave oven? An American engineer called Percy Spencer. In 1945, he was working with radar machines. One day, he had a snack bar in his pocket, and it melted! He was very surprised. Then he put some popcorn near the machine, and it popped. He didn't need much time to understand. These waves could cook food! Today, there are millions of microwave ovens around the world.

articles.title: A Windy Day at Greystone Castle
articles.dek: Sofia climbed a castle tower. Her grandma has a castle story too!
paras: Sofia is thirteen. Last week, her class went on a school trip to Greystone Castle. Read her emails with her grandma.

Hi Grandma, How are you? I'm home again now. Our trip to Greystone Castle was amazing! The bus journey was long, but my friends were with me, so it wasn't boring. When we arrived, the weather was cold and windy. The castle was on a hill above the sea. Its walls were very thick and grey.

Inside, there were lots of dark rooms and narrow stairs. Our guide was a tall man called Mr Okafor. He was really funny. The best part was the tower. There were 150 steps to the top! My legs were tired, but the view was wonderful. Were you ever in a castle when you were young? Love, Sofia

Dear Sofia, Thank you for your lovely email. Yes, I was! When I was ten, my family lived near an old castle in Spain. It wasn't a museum then. It was empty, and the gate was always open. My brother and I were often there after school. We were knights and princesses in our games!

Once, we were inside the castle when a big storm started. It was very dark, and we were scared. We weren't at home for dinner, so our parents were very worried. When we got home, we were wet and dirty. My mother wasn't happy at all! Was there a gift shop at your castle? Love, Grandma

Hi Grandma, What a great story! Yes, there was a small gift shop. The postcards were cheap, so I bought one for you. It's a photo of the tower. It's on the way to you now. Next summer, can we visit your castle in Spain together? Love, Sofia

articles.title: The Missing Speech
articles.dek: Tomás practised his speech all week. Then his cards disappeared.
paras: Tomás was nervous all week. On Friday, he had to give a speech in front of the whole school. The topic was "My hero". He chose his grandfather. His grandfather was a fisherman for forty years.

Every evening, Tomás practised in his bedroom. He wrote his speech on five small cards. He read it to his mum, his dad and even the cat. "You're ready," his dad said on Thursday evening. But Tomás didn't feel ready. That night, he slept badly.

On Friday morning, Tomás got up late. He quickly put on his uniform, took his bag and ran to the bus stop. At school, the hall was full. Hundreds of students sat on chairs and talked loudly. Tomás opened his bag. His heart stopped. The cards weren't there!

He looked in every pocket. He looked under his chair. Nothing. Then he remembered. The cards were still on his bed at home. "What am I going to do?" he thought. His hands started to shake. Then his teacher, Ms Lee, called his name.

Tomás walked slowly to the front. He looked at all the faces. For a moment, he couldn't speak. Then he thought about his grandfather. He thought about the small blue boat and the cold winter mornings at sea. Suddenly, the words came. He didn't need the cards. He knew the story by heart.

Tomás talked for three minutes. He told funny stories about his grandfather, and the students laughed. At the end, everyone clapped. Ms Lee smiled and said, "That was the best speech today." After school, Tomás phoned his grandfather and told him everything. His grandfather laughed. "Next time, forget your cards again!" he said.

grammar.rule: Regular verbs add -ed in the past: walk → walked, practise → practised. Many common verbs are irregular and have a special past form: write → wrote, run → ran. The past form is the same for I, you, he, she, we and they.

He wrote his speech on five small cards.
He quickly put on his uniform, took his bag and ran to the bus stop.
He knew the story by heart.

items.why: Practise is regular and ends in -e, so just add -d.

kps.fact: Tomás had to give a speech called "My hero" about his grandfather.
Tomás practised every evening and wrote his speech on five cards.
On Friday, Tomás left his cards on his bed at home.
Tomás knew his speech by heart, and everyone clapped at the end.
opts: That was the best speech today.

mindmap.question: How did Tomás give his speech without his cards?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the story.
summary.model: Tomás left his speech cards at home, so he was very worried. But he knew the story by heart because he practised a lot.

options.t: Tomás practised his speech about his grandfather every evening.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 1 and 2.
options.evidence: Every evening, Tomás practised in his bedroom.

options.t: On Friday, he found that his cards were at home.
options.why: This is the problem in paragraphs 3 and 4.
options.evidence: The cards were still on his bed at home.

options.t: He gave his speech from memory, and everyone clapped.
options.why: This is how the story ends.

options.t: Tomás read his speech to the cat.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: He read it to his mum, his dad and even the cat.

options.t: Tomás's grandfather came to the school hall.
Tomás slept very well the night before the speech.
